parts.note: a pear is a fruit
main means chief or most important

explanation.surface: A grocer declares which fruit matters most: the apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pearmain is a long-established English variety of eating apple, so an example of the definition.

definitions.meaning: the top or peak of something, its highest point
an ... fare is a cheap advance-purchase ticket for air or rail travel

explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a thing is its apex, and Apex is also a discounted advance-booking ticket class.

clue.text: Set up to continue transporting by water — it's just a short distance

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means each following piece is written upwards, so read backwards in place

parts.note: to carry on is to go on, giving on
to raft is to carry goods by water on a raft

explanation.surface: A boatman sets about continuing to ferry goods, but only a short way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns each piece in place: ON becomes NO and RAFT becomes TFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just a short distance away is close by, an idiomatic way of saying nearby.

clue.text: Jazzy location for inexperienced swimmers about to enter fray

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the other pieces
fray, as in to unravel, tells us to tangle the letters of the preceding words

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced
dolphins are swimmers of the sea

explanation.surface: Novice swimmers are about to plunge into the melee.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures nervous swimmers; 'fray' is the anagram signal, not a fight, and 'about' makes the shuffled letters go round the rest. The plural S of the swimmers starts the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous jazz standard, and the title names a street, hence a jazzy location.

definitions.meaning: booked or held back for someone, as a table is

explanation.definitionFit: A seat held for someone is reserved, and a retiring, undemonstrative person is also described with that word.

clue.text: Religious type: train spotter with a New Testament

indicators.note: to train is to bend or direct into a new shape, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: T for testament, as in NT for New Testament

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is described as a train spotter carrying a copy of the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train spotter' looks like a hobbyist, but 'train' is the anagram signal working on 'spotter', giving PROTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant is a member of a Western Christian church separate from Rome, so a religious type.

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp

indicators.note: new tells us to make something fresh out of the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Wise birds are singing in the New Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a woodland area in southern England; here 'New' is the anagram signal for FOREST SINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These were American heavy bombers of the Second World War, the B-17s.

parts.note: a deep person is crafty or cunning
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A sly county really, whatever it may look like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at heart or in reality, despite how things seem on the surface.

clue.text: Register kept back by chancellor, needlessly

indicators.note: kept back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A finance minister keeps the register back for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' does double service in the surface, but 'by' signals that the letters lie in the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: To register for a course or roll is to sign up, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal

indicators.note: hollow means the word is emptied of its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An antelope is described as truly empty within.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large straight-horned antelope of Africa and Arabia.

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the letters are uncertain and so can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A physicist queries whether light is bent, then answers with total confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean without any doubt; the phrase is a common adverbial synonym.

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: A works supervisor puts a mistake right.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman, especially on a building site.

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
visage is a literary word for face

explanation.surface: Gauge the face in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in your mind is to imagine or foresee it, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: A thankless person (like Cinders?) tearing off

indicators.note: off, as in gone bad or out of order, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Cinderella, ripping her rags, is called ungrateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like Cinders?' gives a second route: cinders lie IN a GRATE, so the answer also splits that way.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is someone who shows no gratitude, an ungrateful person.

clue.text: Tense American hits clumps of grass

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
socks means punches or hits

explanation.surface: A nervous American lashes out at bits of turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense tuft or clump of coarse grass, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Get on with leader from Virginia in Charleston, say?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Charleston is a dance, so this is a dance

indicators.note: leader from means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Making progress, guided by someone from Virginia in a city named Charleston.
explanation.walkthrough: Charleston is also a city in West Virginia, so the surface reads as a place; 'say' shows it is an example of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to go forward or progress, to get on.

clue.text: Wood everyone must break up or break down?

indicators.note: must break says one piece splits the other open

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A forester asks whether everyone in the woods should split up or have a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall apart or suffer a breakdown, physically or mentally.

clue.text: Drink with Midwest journalists going to Ohio

parts.note: the middle letters of the word west
the press means journalists collectively
O is an old abbreviation for the state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Reporters from the American Midwest head to Ohio for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans, a drink.

definitions.meaning: to queer someone's pitch is to spoil or thwart a plan

explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to put an end to it, and Scotch is also whisky.

clue.text: Come to rest somewhere in Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: to land or alight, as dust or a bird does
a market town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to land and stay put, and Settle is also a town in the Yorkshire Dales.

parts.note: gobs are lumps or chunks
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: A confectioner piles lumps of sugar on a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobstopper is a very large, hard round sweet, a British confection.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
raw means bare or naked

explanation.surface: A bishop goes unclothed for a whisky, and how fine it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for 21' points at the Scots: BRAW is a Scottish word, and 21 down is Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect braw means fine, handsome or splendid.
To bolt food is to wolf it down, and to bolt is also to flee suddenly.

definitions.meaning: the American spelling of a bank draft used to pay

explanation.definitionFit: To check is to halt something, and in American spelling it is also the bank order called a cheque in Britain.

clue.text: Boxer that is outwardly a dreamer

indicators.note: outwardly means the first piece sits on the outside of the second

parts.note: id est, Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
Muhammad Ali, the famous boxer

explanation.surface: A fighter, it turns out, is a visionary on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty, often unrealistic ideals, so is something of a dreamer.
